One night, Milo’s grandmother asked him, “What would you do if a star fell from the sky?” Milo’s eyes widened. He imagined a glowing, gentle star, heavy with stories, landing in the bush.  

With a flashlight, he set out at dusk. He found the star, not a rock, but a tiny, shimmering feather that whispered, “Share.” Milo carried it home and, instead of keeping it, he spread it in the garden. The feather fell onto the soil, and soon a sapling grew, taller than any tree Milo had ever seen.  

The lesson Milo learned: the brightest gifts are those shared with others. He kept the feather in his pocket, a reminder that sharing makes the world grow, just like the star that lit his path.  

Goodnight, Milo. Sleep with a heart that shines for others.
